nodes.label: GooseOS Main Desktop
nodes.description: Win95-style desktop environment showing the full GooseOS desktop with wallpaper, icons, and taskbar. Overall composition mimics classic Windows XP Bliss wallpaper aesthetic with rolling green hills and blue sky.

nodes.label: Windows XP Bliss-Style Wallpaper
nodes.description: Background wallpaper is a direct homage to the iconic Windows XP 'Bliss' wallpaper: rolling green grassy hill under a vivid blue sky with scattered white cumulus clouds. Occupies nearly the entire screen real estate behind the icons and taskbar.

nodes.label: Win95-Style Taskbar
nodes.description: Thin horizontal taskbar anchored to the bottom of the screen. Dark/charcoal background color. Contains a Start button labeled './start' on the far left, styled with retro terminal-script syntax ('./start') instead of a traditional 'Start' label, evoking a Unix shell command aesthetic fused with Win95 UI.

nodes.label: Start Button (./start)
nodes.description: The Start button in the bottom-left corner of the taskbar is labeled './start' — a Unix shell script invocation syntax replacing the classic 'Start' label. Small rectangular button with dark background and light text. This is a deliberate design choice merging terminal culture with Win95 UI metaphor.

nodes.label: Desktop Icon: //game.sh
nodes.description: Desktop icon in the upper-left area of the desktop. Icon image appears to be a small humanoid/robot figure (possibly a goose character). Label reads '//game.sh' — using double-slash prefix and .sh extension to frame it as a shell script, reinforcing the Unix-meets-Win95 aesthetic. Links to the affine matrix transformation game.

nodes.label: Desktop Icon: $izePAINT
nodes.description: Desktop icon positioned to the right of the //game.sh icon in the upper area. Icon image is a palette/paint-brush icon with warm orange/yellow tones. Label reads '$izePAINT' — uses a dollar-sign prefix ($ like a shell variable or currency symbol) combined with 'PAINT' evoking MS Paint. This likely links to the goose art upload feature.

nodes.label: Desktop Icon: c:\vibes
nodes.description: Desktop icon on the left column, second row. Label reads 'c:\vibes' — using Windows drive path notation (C:\) combined with the slang term 'vibes', blending retro Windows file path syntax with modern internet culture. Icon appears to be a small folder or file icon.

nodes.label: Desktop Icon: .skynet
nodes.description: Desktop icon on the right column, second row. Label reads '.skynet' — using the Unix dotfile prefix (hidden file convention) combined with 'skynet' (Terminator AI reference). Icon appears to show a small building or tower image. Cultural mash-up of Unix hidden files, Terminator lore, and Win95 aesthetics.

nodes.label: Desktop Icon: ...vote_.(gs)
nodes.description: Desktop icon in the lower-left area of the desktop. Label reads '...vote_.(gs)' — ellipsis prefix suggesting a truncated or mysterious path, 'vote' describing the voting feature, '_.' as separators, and '(gs)' likely referencing 'geese' or the goose theme. Small icon with what appears to be a landscape/image thumbnail. Links to the goose art voting carousel.

nodes.label: Desktop Icon Grid Layout
nodes.description: Icons are arranged in a loose two-column grid on the upper-left quadrant of the desktop, following classic Win95 icon placement convention. Left column: //game.sh (top), c:\vibes (middle), ...vote_.(gs) (bottom). Right column: $izePAINT (top), .skynet (middle). Icons have text labels beneath them in white/light text against the wallpaper.

nodes.label: Icon Label Typography Style
nodes.description: All desktop icon labels use small white text rendered directly over the wallpaper without a drop shadow or background pill, consistent with Win95 icon label rendering. Label text uses a mix of shell/terminal naming conventions: ./ prefix, // prefix, $ prefix, c:\ path notation, dotfile prefix, and parenthetical suffixes.

nodes.label: Overall Color Scheme
nodes.description: Color palette dominated by the wallpaper: vibrant green (grass), bright blue (sky), white (clouds). Taskbar is dark charcoal/near-black providing contrast. Icon images use warm yellows, oranges, greens. Text is white. The palette evokes both Windows XP nostalgia and a slightly surreal, whimsical aesthetic.

nodes.label: Win95 Desktop Metaphor
nodes.description: The entire UI uses the Win95/WinXP desktop metaphor: wallpaper background, desktop icons with labels, and a bottom-anchored taskbar with a start button. This is a deliberate retro-computing aesthetic choice for a modern web application, creating nostalgic UX.

nodes.label: Unix/Terminal Naming Convention for Icons
nodes.description: A distinctive design pattern where all desktop icon labels and the start button use Unix/terminal naming conventions (./, //, $, c:\, dotfiles, .sh extensions, parenthetical suffixes) rather than plain English labels. This creates a fusion aesthetic of Win95 GUI and Unix command-line culture.

nodes.label: Affine Matrix Game Feature (via //game.sh)
nodes.description: The //game.sh icon on the desktop represents the affine matrix transformation game, one of the core features of GooseOS. Accessible from the desktop as a clickable icon.

nodes.label: Goose Art Voting Feature (via ...vote_.(gs))
nodes.description: The ...vote_.(gs) icon on the desktop represents the goose art voting carousel feature, where users can vote on uploaded goose art. Accessible from the desktop as a clickable icon.

nodes.label: Goose Art Upload Feature (via $izePAINT)
nodes.description: The $izePAINT icon on the desktop likely represents the goose art upload feature, referencing MS Paint as a metaphor for art creation/upload. The paint palette icon reinforces this.
